newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to tender for nuclear plant by mid-November.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to tender for nuclear plant by mid-November.

text.p: Turkey will invite international bidders for a tender by mid-November for its first nuclear power plant that will have a capacity of 700 to 1,100 megawatts (MW), a senior energy official said on Wednesday.
Ugur Dogan, undersecretary for the energy ministry, said the tender terms were prepared after consultations with the South Korean Atomic Energy Research Institute.
"We will put the final touches to the tender terms and go out to the tender in early November, likely by mid-November," he told Reuters.
He said the plant, to be at Akkuyu region near the southern port of Mersin, would be financed entirely by the builders, according to the terms.
"We will also require that the builder is an experienced company, whose previous works were tested and proved reliable," he said.
The plant will be operated by the state power producer TEAS, he said.
Turkey, in need of energy and buying electricity from Iran since August, is engaged in a big energy production drive to increase use of gas, thermal and hydraulic resources.
Analysts say the plant, expected to produce about 11 billion kiloWatt-hours annually, may cost about $3 billion and will take about eight years to complete.
The nuclear power plant plan has been on Turkey's agenda for about 30 years, but was long shelved after severe criticism from local residents, politicians and environmentalist activists.
Officials earlier said Turkey was considering another nuclear plant on the Black Sea coast.
